To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• SSL/TLS is not secure, if the protocol is used without any security measures.

the SSL/TLS protocol has been used in a way that is not compliant to the specification, that it has been used in an insecure environment, and that it has not been used with the latest version of the protocol.

• TLS is not a secure protocol, because of the design of its core mechanisms and its flexibility • The security of TLS is only as good as the weakest part of the whole protocol stack • The security of the whole stack is only as good if the whole stack is implemented correctly and securely.
In summary, our research is concerned with
security issues of SSL/TLS, which are not yet resolved.

the following questions: How can we prevent the protocol from being misused? How can we prevent protocol flaws? How can we improve the protocol design? How can we detect protocol flaws? How do we mitigate protocol flaws? How to improve the protocol deployment?
the question ”Why are there so many attacks?”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SSL/TLS is a very complex protocol and that the security is very much dependent on the used cipher suite.
the protocol is too complex, too flexible and too hard to implement correctly.
SSL/TLS is not as secure as expected and that it is not possible to configure it to be secure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SSL/TLS protocol has been developed in a very pragmatic way, without much theoretical background.
SSL/TLS has been proven to be very robust and secure, despite of the attacks.
the SSL/TLS protocol is a complex and hard protocol to get right.
The main takeaway from our work is that
many of the attacks were caused by a lack of understanding the cryptographic primitives and the security goals.
SSL/TLS is a very complex protocol and that the security of SSL/TLS is very hard to reason about.
the SSL/TLS protocol has a long history of security problems, which are not always related to the protocol itself, but rather to the implementations and the way the protocol is used.
